## Problem

Design a distributed system that improves both network utilization and end-to-end processing throughput. Explain the proposed architecture, the technologies you would select, and how the system would manage resources and assign work across its nodes.

_High-level architecture of the distributed job processing system across regions_

![Central services with regional dispatchers and workers](https://cgppcnnkwbfiieexbrea.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/diagrams/daed2b4a4ca8752313291bf9bab8952e.svg)



## Constraints

- The design must support multiple geographic regions.
- Work should be distributable across independent worker nodes.
- The system should account for both network bandwidth and compute capacity when placing tasks.
- A single node or regional failure must not stop all processing.
- The design must explain how tasks are queued, scheduled, monitored, retried, and reassigned when necessary.
- The technology stack and its role in the architecture must be identified.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Focus on data locality and minimizing cross-node communication, use a distributed scheduler that assigns tasks to nodes where the data resides.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Consider a master-worker architecture with a central coordinator that monitors node load and network latency to balance work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The key trade-off is between centralized control (simpler but a bottleneck) and decentralized scheduling (more complex but scalable).

</details>
